rv.q: A Walk on the Moon is a pleasant trip.
The wonderful cast gives A Walk on the Moon its liftoff.
Now that it’s arrived, it deserves to stick around way past the summer.
But as both a period piece and a musical, A Walk on the Moon never captures the emotional or cultural excitement of 1969.
And yet, to my surprise, too much of “A Walk on the Moon,” opening tonight Off-Broadway, strikes me as dated and dull.
By the end, we don’t comprehend why this woman embarked on a fling with a stranger, why she regretted it, or how that experience might have changed her, for good or otherwise.
AnnMarie Milazzo's score is emotionally accessible and filled with hooks that linger long after leaving the theatre.
This is an affable, nostalgic, empathetic piece with little artistic distinction.

cn.t: This nostalgic musical adaptation of the 1999 film receives mixed reviews, with critics finding it blandly entertaining but overly familiar. Some praise its energy and period atmosphere, while others cite disappointing execution and clichés.
